description: Change a panel on a board: its title, how it draws, its number format or what it shows. Pass only what changes; the rest stays as it is. The panel id is in get_board. To turn it into another type, pass `type` with the full spec for it, the same fields as add_panel. A changed panel is run and held to the same rules as add_panel before it is saved (structured types before SQL, one question per panel, the board's time range), and one that breaks them is refused with nothing changed.

chart.description: For trends: line (default) over time; area for a total made of parts over time (stacked with `display.stacked`); bar to compare segments over time; hbar to rank segments by their total (long names, top pages, plans); share for each segment's part of the whole (a breakdown over the window, up to six slices); heatmap for when one series happens across the week (weekday × hour, UTC; one series, no breakdown); scalar for one number; table for rows. For retention: table (default, the cohort grid) or line (the average curve). For sql: table (default), line or bar.

display.description: How the panel reads. format, stacked and legend are for trends and sql; thresholds and note for any panel but text.

format.description: currency for money, percent for a rate; default count.

legend.description: Line charts: show the legend. Default true.

note.description: One plain sentence under the title on how to read the panel or what changed. Your own words, never captured data.

stacked.description: Bar charts with several series: stack them. Default true.

thresholds.description: Up to five values the user named to read the panel against (a target, a limit, an error budget). A chart draws each as a dashed line in its colour; a number takes the colour of the highest one it has reached. Only values the user gave; never invent one.

color.description: green at the target, red at the limit, amber for a warning before it, blue to mark a level without judging it.

value.description: In the panel's own unit: 0.25 for 25% with format percent.

breakdown.description: {scope, key}. scope "event" = payload property, "context" = built-in dimension (country, browser, page_path, utm_source…), "session", "user" = user trait.

conversionWindow.description: How long an entrant has to finish, e.g. {value: 1, unit: "day"}. Default 1 day.
